body.statement: For every tie face \(A\) with \(|A|\geq2\) and positive \(v_A\), define \(s_A(p)=\sum_{k\in A}(Bp)_k\), \(a_A(p)=(Bp)_A/s_A(p)\), and \(s_{A,\max}=\max_\ell\sum_{k\in A}B_{k\ell}\). Then \(G_A(v_A,(Bp)_A)=s_A(p)^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,a_A(p))\) and \[\frac{R_{B,A}^\star(v_A)}{R_{CR,A}^\star(v_A)}\geq s_{A,\max}^{-1/2}>1.\] Equality in this lower ratio holds exactly when there exists a Bernoulli optimizer \(p\) supported on columns attaining \(s_{A,\max}\) whose normalized active vector \(a_A(p)\) is exact-count optimal. Inactive coordinates may be zero and are never passed to \(G_A\).
body.proof_tex:
By \(\texttt{lem:gaussian-information-order}\), the Gaussian game is homogeneous and coordinatewise nonincreasing in information.  Since \((Bp)_A=s_A(p)a_A(p)\),
\[
G_A(v_A,(Bp)_A)=s_A(p)^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,a_A(p)). \tag{43}
\]
For each label \(\ell\), \(\sum_{k\in A}B_{k\ell}\) is the probability that \(\operatorname{Bin}(n,\pi_\ell)\) belongs to the proper target-count set \(\{m_k:k\in A\}\).  Interior \(\pi_\ell\) and exclusion of counts zero and \(n\) imply
\[
0<s_A(p)\leq s_{A,\max}<1. \tag{44}
\]
Moreover \(a_A(p)\in\Delta_A^\circ\).  The definition of \(R_{CR,A}^\star\) and (43)--(44) give, for every \(p\),
\[
G_A(v_A,(Bp)_A)\geq s_{A,\max}^{-1/2}R_{CR,A}^\star(v_A). \tag{45}
\]

Both minima are attained.  The image \((B\Delta_K)_A\) is compact and bounded away from all active coordinate hyperplanes.  The relative-rate modulus in the information-order lemma makes \(G_A\) continuous there.  On \(\Delta_A\), the lower-semicontinuous extension attains its minimum; it is finite at the uniform allocation and infinite on the boundary, so every exact-count minimizer is in \(\Delta_A^\circ\).  The two-arm lower bound in that lemma makes \(R_{CR,A}^\star>0\).  Taking minima in (45), dividing by this positive value, and using (44) proves the displayed strict ratio.

If equality holds, take a Bernoulli minimizer \(p^\star\).  Both gaps in
\[
s_A(p^\star)^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,a_A(p^\star))
\geq s_{A,\max}^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,a_A(p^\star))
\geq s_{A,\max}^{-1/2}R_{CR,A}^\star
\]
must vanish.  Strict positivity forces \(s_A(p^\star)=s_{A,\max}\), and the second equality makes \(a_A(p^\star)\) exact-count optimal.  A convex combination of column masses reaches their maximum exactly when supported on maximizing columns.  This proves necessity.  Conversely, such support and an exact-count-optimal normalized vector turn both inequalities into equalities, proving sufficiency.  Only active coordinates enter the face game.
body.justification: This is the sole field-level headline: a sharp optimized information-loss frontier for the same exact-count causal target. BasseFeller2018 is the direct two-stage exact-count benchmark for the competing fixed-count regime, while HudgensHalloran2008 supplies the partial-interference setting in which isolated cluster schedules make that comparison causal. HiranoPorter2009, Stoye2009, Joo2025, and Kato2026 provide adjacent minimax-regret or Gaussian-selection foundations, but none supplies the observed-law exact-hit information map, its all-rule deletion reduction, or the Bernoulli-versus-exact-count frontier. MogstadRomanoShaikhWilhelm2024 and BazylikMogstadRomanoShaikhWilhelm2025 instead motivate the supporting tie-valid rank-inference consequence. Its non-overlap with the accepted experimentation-bank kernels is substantive: exp_multiarm_secondorder_minimax_frontier studies fixed-arm finite-population contrast MSE and its second-order n^(-4/3) frontier, not clustered exact-slice welfare or a Bernoulli-hit versus exact-count mechanism comparison; exp_design_pm1_exactness_boundary certifies plus-minus-one implementability of a homophily covariance-SDP relaxation, not target-hit information or simple-regret ranking.
body.gap: Prior saturation-design papers do not provide this all-rule facewise equality frontier. BasseFeller2018 analyzes two-stage interference experiments but does not price the loss from nominal Bernoulli labels relative to exact-count allocation for this welfare-selection target; HudgensHalloran2008 supplies the interference framework rather than a design-information comparison. HiranoPorter2009 and Stoye2009 supply decision-theoretic foundations, while Joo2025 and Kato2026 concern Gaussian or sequential selection architectures rather than this observed exact-hit experiment and outer hit polytope. MogstadRomanoShaikhWilhelm2024 and BazylikMogstadRomanoShaikhWilhelm2025 address rank-set inference rather than the simple-regret mechanism frontier. In particular, the accepted-bank multiarm minimax result neither has the unrestricted iid cluster-schedule model, the exact-count welfare estimand, nor the hit map q=Bp; the accepted-bank plus-minus-one design result neither compares Bernoulli labels with complete randomization nor has a tie-face Gaussian selection game. Thus neither supplies the mechanism-loss equality criterion or its cluster-count implication.
body.consumer: It lower-bounds clusters required by Bernoulli implementation at any partial tie. For a Basse--Feller-style two-stage experiment under Hudgens--Halloran partial interference, it tells a prospective designer how much first-stage Bernoulli labeling can cost relative to exact-count allocation; the calibrated CLT and the Mogstad--Romano--Shaikh--Wilhelm/Bazylik--Mogstad--Romano--Shaikh--Wilhelm rank-set results remain supporting reporting tools rather than substitutes for the simple-regret comparison.
